## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The timestamp does not match its documented meaning, and the NULL description contradicts the supplied event history. These should be corrected before relying on the new column.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — For process 20, whose only event is `started`, the expression exposes its start timestamp as `finished_at`. Populate this column from the event that denotes completion, or rename it to describe the timestamp actually returned. — Consumers receive a completion timestamp for a process with no completion event.
- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — “NULL means the process has never been started” contradicts `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end`: process 30 has a `started` event followed by `cleared`, so its latest row returns NULL despite having started. Describe NULL according to the latest-event behavior. — Consumers following the catalog will misclassify previously started processes.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- The existing ranking and filter continue to select one row per process using the greatest event ID.
